theme: Sign frequency in context, motif concentration and seal standardization
question: Do top-sign frequencies vary by site size or function beyond object composition; are motif concentration and text differences consistent across contexts; how variable are recorded seal dimensions? The post-launch lecture amendment also asks whether inventories exceed a shared sample-size curve, concentration matches the lecture, 740 is terminal, motifs persist across interval-dated Harappa phases, and Gaur dominates external finds.
outcome: 5,680 faces form 4,695 physical components. Sign 740 is 1,928/19,946 positions; its object-conditioned site q is 0.5379, while sign 032 has q 0.002 across ten signs. No sign's area association survives the amended grouped law across 17 sites (ten have fewer than 20 readable objects). Known square motifs are 1,246/1,609 unicorn, HHI 0.605434. Unicorn versus rare clean texts average 4.794505 versus 4.019355 positions, q 0.0012; sign-distribution divergence fails exact-length conditioning, exploratory q 0.20525. Complete square-seal size n=1,027, CV 0.288599; adjusted length/area slope 1.158998 positions per doubling, q 0.0002. All five analytical outputs and the supplement reproduce; 149 checks pass, zero fail, with 108 reference tails recomputed. Post-launch amendment (Exploratory): no corrected richness outlier among eight sites, minimum q 0.177867. All-face readable top-3/top-6/top-20 shares are 18.6417/27.5143/48.7629 percent; unique-text readable shares are 18.2844/25.1666/46.4945 percent. Terminal 740 is 874/1,256 occurrences in 2,497 clean texts; expected ending objects 299.082 against 874 observed, excess 23.0243 points (95% whole-object interval 21.5005 to 24.4975); TAB:I context q 0.158466. Harappa 203 known Period-3 square motifs have raw-label heterogeneity q 0.007 and interval-time q 0.0194. The 720 dating assignments yield an at-least-95% C-minus-B change envelope of -24.8600 to +85.7669 points; the dated scope spans 700 years. Core known motifs are 1,236/1,604 unicorn; external known motifs 15/27 Gaur, including 13/13 known external circular motifs. Type-conditioned q values are 0.0094 for unicorn geography and 0.0105 for Gaur; restricted Gulf/Mesopotamia Gaur q 0.0172. New verifier: 760 passes, zero failures; original endpoints preserved.
challenge: Published area anchors differ in extent and date; open bounds lack maxima; functional contrasts are represented by one port, craft and rural site each. Sparse site precision affects area references, text length affects motif inventories, and catalogue rounding/range dimensions affect size interpretation. Full style/size precedents and the requested Rao motif item remain unverified. The exact Wells percentage/inventory tables were not opened. Interval-logistic early coverage rests on one 3A motif; ambiguous dating allows substantial changes. Export regions include Indus-peripheral Balochistan in the Iranian Plateau external proxy, and Gaur codes remain unverified against photographs.
remedy: Preserved a pre-outcome protocol and source table; grouped complete object payloads inside type/site blocks; corrected across specified outcomes; retained both original and dated exploratory reference laws; excluded zero/range scalar dimensions with a local audit; saved witnesses and failures locally; wrote source notes and deterministic verification without changing shared files. A dated post-launch amendment preceded new computation; archived living documents, exact token/object-preserving blocks, bounded rarefaction/extrapolation, exact object-anchor tails, interval likelihood and exhaustive dating allocations, restricted geographic sensitivity and a local-only external list preserve reviewability. The failed partial serialization run is retained. After the user-reported disk-full interruption, all 1,850 recorded files remained intact, with 1,849 size/hash matches. The recovery audit found no format or link errors; only a regenerable font cache was removed. No statistical run or source download was repeated.
retry_when: Contemporaneous occupied-site areas and excavation denominators are available; small sites and minority motifs have substantially larger independent samples; original calibrated seal dimensions and workshop/carving-style assignments can test predefined size classes; unread direct precedents and the Rao motif item have been obtained. For lecture claims, obtain the precise Wells corpus tables, larger independently dated early-phase motif samples, original find-context denominators and an image-reviewed external motif inventory with site-level geographic classification.
